rationale: A wins because it keeps the founder honest about what can and cannot be pitched today. Its best line is the discipline in “No supplied current news signal pegs this to a breaking moment,” while B starts selling vapor with “utilities are already paying AI to manage it” and then pretends a paid pilot is market adoption. B has real newsroom instincts, but it cannot stop improving the facts it was handed.
gaps_in_A: “someone who ran systems inside Tesla Energy” invents role seniority and scope; the update only says ex-Tesla Energy.
“Community-solar grids are hitting a load-balancing wall” states the trend as proven before supplying independent evidence.
“software is the cheap fix being tried” adds an economics claim the update does not support.
“the fund's name (you have it; I don't)” is a wobbly assumption; the provided facts do not name the lead fund.
gaps_in_B: “utilities are already paying AI to manage it” overstates three unnamed paying pilots into verified utility adoption.
“not just evaluating it” is flatly sloppy; a pilot is evaluation, even if paid.
“An ex-Tesla Energy engineer and an ex-NREL researcher” invents founder roles not in the update.
“Rooftop and community solar were sold as an easy win” drags rooftop solar and a broad advocacy narrative into a fact pattern about community solar only.
